structure: eye diameter as percentage of head length
measurement: eye diameter 19.3–25.3% of head length (range in the species Description; eyes not reduced)
method: percentage range printed in the Description of a new species; the paper's Materials and methods say only that most counts and morphometric measurements followed Tang et al. (2012) and that measurements were made with digital calipers to the nearest 0.1 mm; it does not define eye diameter or head length, so this is filed as sensory_anatomy, not eye_diameter_mm
conditions: Preserved type material of a new cave-region loach from Guangxi. Holotype NNNU230611, 41.2 mm standard length, China: Guangxi, Wuming County, Chuanqian Village, collected by H.L. Mo and J.H. Zhong in June 2023. The Description does not say which specimens the range covers; the Materials list the holotype plus paratypes (paratypes NNNU230603–230610, 8 ex., 26.1–33.4 mm standard length). In the Description the eye sentence comes after the nostril sentences ('Anterior and posterior nostrils adjacent; ...') and before the barbel sentence ('Three pairs of barbels: ...'); the fetch tool returned the Description in pieces and the order is as read there. The paper's Diagnosis for either species has no eye or interorbital sentence (tool report). Other eye wording read through the tool: Discussion 'such as eye degeneration or loss, reduced pigmentation, and diminished scales.' (general, no species figure); Table 1 rows 'Head height at eye' and 'Head width at eye' (tool listed no eye-diameter row; table not opened cell by cell); the barbel sentence mentions the posterior margin of the eye. No other eye-diameter sentence for this species was returned. The other species in the paper, P. liui, has 17.3%–21.9% (filed separately).
